MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  November 17, 2014

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Kelley at 5:00 p.m., on November 17, 2014, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on November 12, 2014, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman
P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Reardon
  Council Member Schlicht (arrived at 5:04 p.m.)
  Council Member Ury
  Mayor Pro Tem Leckness
  Mayor Kelley

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Legal Counsel--Anticipated Litigation Based on existing facts and
  circumstances, the Successor Agency, City Council, and Financing Authority will
  confer with legal counsel and provide direction regarding (i) whether or not to initiate
  litigation pursuant to Section 54956.9(c) - one potential case, and (ii) significant
  exposure to litigation pursuant to Section 54956.9(d) - one potential case.

City Council Minutes  1  November 17, 2014
 RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour 5:01 p.m., Mayor Kelley declared a recess to Closed Session. The City Council
reconvened at 6:00 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Pro Tem Leckness

INVOCATION: Council Member Reardon

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the Council directed staff to comply with State
Department of Finance direction so the City will be moving forward with the subject development
project accordingly.

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Adopted Headquarters Battalion of the 1st Marine Division Quarterly Recognition

  Mayor Kelley presented certificates of commendation to "Marine of the Quarter" Lance
  Corporal Nicholas Eble and "Noncommissioned Officer of the Quarter" Sergeant Ryan
  Kincaid.

P2.  Featured Business of the Month - Atria del Sol

  Mayor Kelley presented the proclamation to Laura Kephart, Manager of Atria del Sol.

P3.  Recognize Anna T. Boyce as a Hometown Hero

  Mayor Kelley presented the proclamation to Anna T. Boyce.

P4.  Update on the Refinancing of the San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency

  Transportation Corridor Agencies CFO Amy Potter made the presentation.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Bob Hayes, M.V.: presented the City Council with information on the Honor Flight Program and
suggested that the City support it by scheduling a presentation by co-founders Craig Van Doren
and Luci Miller. He also recommended that the Community of Character Committee, veterans
groups and civic organizations actively support the program.

City Council Minutes  2  November 17, 2014
 Carole Weidler, Casta del Sol liaison, M.V.: thanked the City Council, especially those who are
retiring, for their leadership, strength in the face of often brutal criticism, and staunch
determination to keep the city safe. She stated that it is obvious as one looks around Mission Viejo
that they have done their jobs well.

Margot Ferron, M.V.: speaking on behalf of the Friends of the Arts and the Cultural Arts
Committee, she invited the Council and the community to the unveiling of the R. Hero Sculpture
at La Paws Dog Park. The artwork was donated to the City by the Hero Foundation whose mission
is to honor first responders. The sculpture will be unveiled on Saturday, November 22, beginning
at 10:00 a.m.

Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: reiterated his disappointment in Mayor Pro Tem Leckness for voting
to approve the OCFA firefighters’ contract after receiving a campaign contribution from the
Firefighters union. He apologized at the last meeting after hearing that was untrue however, since
then, Mr. Wontrobski said his research of campaign filings revealed that Mr. Leckness reported a
$1,500 OCFA contribution on October 8 and another one on October 14, 2014. Mayor Pro Tem
Leckness responded that he did not receive $3,000 in donations but one donation of $1,500.

Robert D. Breton, M.V.: thanked the City Council Members for the fine job that they have been
doing. He noted that he serves on the Grand Jury and as they look across the county, it is almost
universally accepted that Mission Viejo sets the bar and the gold standard in so many areas. Mr.
Breton stated that he was particularly impressed with two recent events that made him very proud
to be a resident: the Veterans Day devotional celebration and the International Wheelchair Tennis
Tournament.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 3, 4, 5, and 15 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.

Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, to approve the
Consent Calendar as described below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said title
  which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further
  reading waived.

City Council Minutes  3  November 17, 2014
 2.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of November 3, 2014, as
  presented.

6.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for September 2014

  Received and filed.

7.  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly
  Report for September 2014

  Received and filed.

8.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing  Authority  (MVCDFA)
  Treasurer’s Monthly Report for September 2014

  Received and filed.

9.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for
  September 2014

  Received and filed.

10.  Library Holiday Schedule for 2015 Calendar Year

  Approved proposed Library Holiday and Closure Schedule for 2015.

11.  Federal-Aid Highway Safety Improvement Program (HSIP) Grant: Citywide
  Emergency Vehicle Pre-Emption (EVP) System Installation Project (CIP 215)

  Awarded the construction contract in the amount of $386,669 to Macadee Electrical
  Construction, Inc., to install 65 emergency vehicle pre-emption devices on existing traffic
  signal infrastructure.

12.  2015 Orange County International Triathlon in Mission Viejo

  Approved the request submitted by Pelican Coast Events, LLC, to hold the 2015 Orange
  County International Triathlon in Mission Viejo on Sunday, June 7, 2015.

City Council Minutes  4  November 17, 2014
 13.  Mission Viejo Animal Shelter Cattery Expansion Project - CIP 318

  (1) Authorized the City Clerk to record Notice of Completion with the County of Orange
  and to release the faithful performance and payment bonds one year and 35 days
  respectively after the date of recordation of the Notice of Completion contingent upon no
  claims or liens being filed with or by the City; and (2) authorized the payment to IBN
  Construction Inc., of the final retention of $19,381.35, 35 days after the date of recordation
  of the Notice of Completion.

14.  Request by the Mission Viejo Activities Committee for a one-time exemption to the
  "No Alcoholic Beverage Consumption" Regulation at City facilities

  Approved the request by the Mission Viejo Activities Committee for a one-time exemption
  to the "No Alcoholic Beverage Consumption" Regulation at City facilities.

16.  Amendment to Salary Schedule and Authorized Positions Schedule

  (1) Adopted Resolution 14-52 Amending the City's Salary Schedule and Establishing Salary
  Ranges for Authorized Job Classifications; and (2) adopted Resolution 14-53 Amending
  the City's Authorized Positions Schedule for FY 14/15.

OLD BUSINESS

NEW BUSINESS

17.  Community Services Funding Program - Funding for Fiscal Year 2014-2015

  Community Services Supervisor Leslie Rae-McDonald presented the staff report and
  answered the City Council Members questions.

  Council Member Schlicht stated for the record that she is opposed to taxpayer funds being
  used for social programs for the arts and she would rather give the money to the school
  district to fund the music programs that are often cut to meet budget problems. She also
  noted that a new Obama rule could force cities to house illegal aliens.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Reardon, to approve
  the Community Services Commission's recommended funding amounts for Fiscal Year
  2014-2015 for the Community Services Funding Program.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None
City Council Minutes  5  November 17, 2014
 ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

3.  Check Register Dated October 24, 2014 in the Amount of $2,035,353.92

  Council Member Schlicht inquired about payments made to CQ Productions for Curiosity
  Quest Goes Green, Gail Shiomoto-Lohr for professional services, Tom Bistline
  Construction for sandbags, and travel expenses for Tyler Technologies.

  Staff provided responses where available and agreed to get back to the City Council with
  details as necessary.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Mayor Kelley, to ratify the
  accompanying check register.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

4.  Check Register Dated October 31, 2014 in the Amount of $2,406,189.32

  Council Member Schlicht expressed her protest regarding a payment to Aaron Schmidt for
  library website consulting because, she said, the Council is the Library Board of Trustees
  yet the Council Members have no input. She also inquired about a payment to Outback
  Steakhouse for the Veterans luncheon and she asked if there was an opportunity for a
  Mission Viejo restaurant to provide the food.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Reardon, to
  ratify the accompanying check register.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

5.  Agreement to Provide Disaster-Related Debris Management and Recovery Services

  Emergency Services Manager Paul Catsimanes presented the staff report and answered the
  City Council Member's questions. Council Member Schlicht expressed concern about
  information that she found on the Internet regarding Ashbritt, Inc.

City Council Minutes  6  November 17, 2014
   Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, to (1)
  authorize the City Manager to execute the Agreement with Ashbritt, Inc. to Provide
  Disaster-Related Debris Removal and Recovery Services; and (2) execute the County of
  Orange Indemnification Supplement.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

15.  Purchase Replacement Cardio Equipment for the Montanoso Recreation Center and
  Sierra Recreation Center

  Community Services Supervisor Andrew Fine presented the staff report and answered the
  City Council Member's questions.

  Motion made by Council Member Reardon, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, to
  authorize the purchase of replacement cardio equipment for the Montanoso Recreation
  Center and Sierra Recreation Center in the amount of $35,496.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Reardon, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

18.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: expressed dissatisfaction with fire chiefs making $400,000 per
  year in total compensation. He stated that he hopes that the City will have a strong
  representative on the OCFA Board in the coming year who will help put an end to these
  exorbitant salaries.

  Mayor Kelley presented the report.

19.  Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Council Member Reardon presented the report.

City Council Minutes  7  November 17, 2014
 20.  San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Council Member Reardon presented the report.

21.  Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA)

  Council Member Ury presented the report.

22.  SCAG Transportation Committee (TC) Report

  Mayor Kelley presented the report.

STAFF REPORTS

23.  Consideration of Approving and Adopting PACE Funding Programs

  City Attorney Bill Curley presented the staff report.

  The following spoke in support of the PACE funding programs: Jan Shomaker, M.V.

  The following presented pros and cons on the PACE programs: Dennis O'Connor, Orange
  County Association of Realtors, M.V.; Brad Turpin, Mortgage Broker, Rancho Santa
  Margarita.

  The following spoke in opposition to the City's adoption of a PACE Funding Program:
  Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.; Steve Magdziak, M.V.; Anthony S. Elia, M.V.

  Dustin Reilich from Hero Program and Jeremy Hutman from CaliforniaFirst answered the
  City Council Members questions.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Reardon, to table this
  matter to the 2nd meeting in January after the new City Council Members have been seated.

  On roll call, said motion failed by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley and Ury
  NOES:  Leckness, Reardon, and Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, seconded by Council Member Schlicht, to deny
  the proposal for PACE Funding Programs in the City of Mission Viejo.

City Council Minutes  8  November 17, 2014
   On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Leckness, Reardon, and Schlicht
  NOES:  Kelley and Ury
  ABSENT:  None

RECESS

At the hour of 8:37 p.m., Mayor Kelley declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 8:46
p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

24.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Reardon

Council Member Reardon asked if resident and realtor Dennis O’Connor could provide his
expertise on the Special Fire Protection Area (SFPA.) Mayor Kelley expressed her preference that
Council Member Reardon be the one to talk about the matter, rather than having a public speaker
during Council Comments.

Council Member Reardon discussed the recent misinformation that has been circulating about
Casta del Sol government affairs manager Carole Weidler. A resident accused Mrs. Weidler of
stating that there was no disclosure required for fire hazard severity zones at the Casta del Sol
candidate forum. Council Member Reardon clarified that the resident making the accusation was
not even present at the forum and Mrs. Weidler did not say that. Instead, Mrs. Weidler said that
residents are not required to disclose the Special Fire Protection Area unless they choose to do
so. Council Member Reardon noted that when an individual purchases a home they must sign a
natural hazard disclosure document and that requirement has been in effect for decades. She stated
that the hazard document refers to a third party to identify hazards in the city and the document
does not list fire hazard severity zones in Mission Viejo because the city does not have
any. Council Member Reardon stated that Mission Viejo is exempt from the fire maps and has
been since June of 2012 and she reiterated that there are no fire hazard severity zones in Mission
Viejo. The disclosure document requires a signature but it doesn’t mean that the homeowner
agrees with everything, it just means that they have received the document. Council Member
Reardon stated that this has been an issue for over 2 years and the Council needs to make sure that
they tell the truth and state the facts when talking about the SFPA. She referenced a letter written
by the City Attorney on the subject and she asked that the letter be distributed to local realtors.

City Council Minutes  9  November 17, 2014
 Council Member Reardon outlined her attendance at recent events including the ITF Wheelchair
Tennis Masters, the City’s Veterans Day ceremony, the Casta del Sol Veterans honor ball and the
Veterans Day ceremony at El Toro Memorial Cemetery. She also participated in a Carl Hankey
School fundraiser and spoke to a Mission Viejo High School humanities class on election matters
and understanding party platforms. Council Member Reardon further discussed her attendance at
a luncheon for the Explorer program, the Fairhaven Memorial’s awards program for caregivers
and an Eagle Scout Court of Honor. Council Member Reardon announced that she attended the
volunteer awards banquet for AYSO Region 84 and she outlined the names of the winners. In
conclusion, she reminded residents of the City’s new drug free web page and she recommended
the four-part video series that is available on the site at www.cityofmissionviejo.org/drugfree.

Council Member Schlicht

Council Member Schlicht announced that she has received many phone calls and congratulations
as if she had been running for office. She stated that her philosophy is to have open and transparent
government and that not everything is decided before the meeting. She believes it is wrong to
expect Council Members to ask questions before the meetings and she stated that she is looking
forward to future projects being done on a needed basis not on a wanted basis. Council Member
Schlicht said that she looks forward to addressing long-term objectives such as solutions to the
$20 million unfunded liability and figuring out where to come up with $7 million shortfall in the
asset replacement funds. Council Member Schlicht thanked residents for the good wishes and she
acknowledged their support. She concluded her comments with a quote from John Adams on the
Rule of Law: “They define a republic to be a government of laws and not of men.”

Council Member Ury

Council Member Ury announced that he had nothing to report.

Mayor Pro Tem Leckness

Mayor Pro Tem Leckness thanked his colleagues and staff and stated that he has enjoyed working
with them over the past five years. He complimented staff and noted that they could not be better
at what they do.

Mayor Kelley

Mayor Kelley commended city staff for a fantastic Veterans Day event. She remembered that in
2002, when she was first elected, the program had about 20 attendees and this year, the community
center’s Sycamore Room was filled. She stated that it was a fantastic event and it is wonderful
that the city can recognize veterans; those who have served in the past and those who are on active
duty. She also commended staff for a fantastic wheelchair tennis event. She attended three times
and her grandchildren were absolutely captivated watching the athletes perform. She said that the
kids had really good, thoughtful questions and it was a great lesson in perseverance and
overcoming one’s life situations. She also noted that this year, staff added a family carnival and
it was a nice supplement to the event. Mayor Kelley reminded residents that the R. Hero dog park
sculpture will be unveiled on Saturday, November 22 at 10:00 a.m. and she congratulated the three
City Council Minutes  10  November 17, 2014
 incoming Council Members, Greg Raths, Ed Sachs and Wendy Bucknum who will be assuming
office at the next City Council Meeting. She outlined the order of the agenda for that meeting at
which time she, Council Member Reardon and Mayor Pro Tem Leckness will be stepping
down. She stated that she appreciated her time working with Council Members Ury and Schlicht
and although they agreed most of the time, they sometimes had differences which she did not mind
because having a diversity of opinions makes for a healthy Council. Mayor Kelley thanked City
staff and stated that they are absolutely the best. She also thanked the residents of Mission Viejo
for electing her to office for three terms and she conveyed that she is pleased that a lot has been
accomplished in those 12 years. Lastly, Mayor Kelley thanked Council Members Reardon and
Leckness for their service. She noted that both of them gave up a lot of time and put their heart
into the job and she is looking forward to the opportunity all three of them will have to make
outgoing comments at the next meeting.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 9:20 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Kelley adjourned the meeting to Monday, December 1, 2014, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of December 1, 2014

City Council Minutes  11  November 17, 2014
